_about: Committed baseline floors for the retrieval eval gate (VER-191) and the two-axis verdict gate. Moving any number here is a deliberate, reviewed act: raise a floor when quality ratchets up, or lower one only with the reason recorded in the PR (see README.md, 'Updating the baseline'). retrieval floors gate the deterministic lexical retrieval oracle's recall@1 over the French political/statistical golden cases (overall and per category); recall@3 is reported but not gated. verdict floors mirror the two-axis literal/flag accuracy the verify-path gate enforces (a drift-guard test binds them to the code constants). The paraphrase floor is below 1.0 on purpose: a purely lexical baseline mis-ranks a reworded claim that shares no distinctive number or entity with its evidence, exactly the gap the upcoming hybrid dense+lexical retrieval must close. gate floors (VER-225) replay the committed check-worthiness fixture (gate_golden.json, regenerated by the training pipeline): cascade accuracy over the golden labels, outside-band agreement with the recorded generative-gate verdicts, and the maximum fraction of statements still routed to the generative model. nli floors (VER-228) replay the committed stance fixture (nli_golden.json, regenerated by the training pipeline's nli-calibrate): accuracy of locally-decided verdicts, the local-decision share, and the hard invariant that a claim and its negation never receive the same stance. budget ceilings (VER-230) compose the predicted generative calls per checked claim from the gate and nli fixtures (gate in-band share + NLI escalation share + weak-local-verdict second-pass share) and fail CI when the total exceeds the committed ceiling; decomposition stays one call per spoken unit by design and is outside this ratio.
